exposure: maternal age group (adolescent 13-19 years vs. adult 20-35 years)
cohort: The study included 60 pregnant women delivering in a tertiary care center, equally divided into adolescent (13-19 years) and adult (20-35 years) age groups.
finding: Teenage mothers had significantly higher illiteracy and lower socioeconomic status, poorer antenatal care utilization, and their neonates had significantly lower mean birth weight, higher incidence of low birth weight, and lower APGAR scores at 1 minute compared to adult mothers.
cross-section timing: Over one year at a tertiary hospital.
birth_weight: Mean birth weight for neonates of teenage mothers was 2.45 +/- 0.38 kg, and for adult mothers was 2.88 +/- 0.36 kg.
